_comment: LAB / EDUCATIONAL - offline DNS fixture for zero-rating-detection-lab.
This file replaces the DNS resolver when lab_config.RESOLVER_MODE == 'fixture'
(the default). It exists so the lab is fully self-contained and deterministic:
running the demo emits ZERO DNS queries and depends on nothing outside this
None of these are real published addresses. Every entry is either loopback or
which is reserved for exactly this purpose and is not routed on the Internet.
127.0.0.2  = where the lab origin serves the GENUINE zero-rated service.
In the fixtures below it stands in for 'the nearest CDN edge
that this subscriber's resolver would have returned'.
127.0.0.1  = where the lab origin serves ordinary chargeable content, and
where the spoofing client actually connects while claiming to
be talking to a zero-rated host.
The extra documentation addresses on each zero-rated host are not decoration:
they make each entry a MULTI-ADDRESS set, which is what forces the detector to
compare against a full resolved set rather than a single 'the' IP. That is the
primary false-positive control for CDN-hosted services.
_unresolvable_note: Any hostname NOT listed above resolves to an empty set. If such a host is
also on the zero-rating whitelist, the detector returns
ZERO_RATING_UNVERIFIABLE at LOW confidence and ALLOWS the flow - it never
treats 'I could not resolve this' as evidence of fraud. Add
'unverifiable.zoom.us' to ZERO_RATED_HOSTS-adjacent traffic to see that path.
